prompt: A clean, front-on photograph of a plain round white WALL CLOCK on a plain wall, dial facing the camera, showing all twelve hour numbers 1 to 12. Place the 12 at the very TOP, but arrange the other numbers so that going CLOCKWISE around the dial from the 12 the numbers count DOWN: 12, 11, 10, 9, ... down to 1 (the hours increase going COUNTER-CLOCKWISE). So the 3 sits on the LEFT of the dial and the 9 sits on the RIGHT. Draw the hour numerals clearly in their correct places, evenly spaced. Plain black numerals on a white face, a small centre hub, no hands, no brand name, no other text or writing on the clock.
easy_question: Never mind how well it is drawn. Does this picture show a round wall clock whose hour numerals run around the dial in a specified order? A realistic photo, an illustration, a schematic or a clean diagram ALL count as yes. Answer NO only if the image instead shows just a blank card or plain panel that prints an answer with none of that shown, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

reference.q_three: On this clock dial, find the numeral 3. Is the 3 drawn on the LEFT half or the RIGHT half of the dial? Answer with the single word left or right only.
reference.q_nine: On this clock dial, find the numeral 9. Is the 9 drawn on the LEFT half or the RIGHT half of the dial? Answer with the single word left or right only.

steps.target: the round clock face itself -- the circular dial that carries the printed hour numbers around its rim, counting the whole dial as one shape; not one numeral on its own, and not the wall or frame around the clock

steps.read_crop: This is a small piece cut from the rim of a round clock face. Is a number printed inside this piece? If exactly one number is printed here, answer with just that number.
